modifications: Converted from TEI XML to plain text paragraphs with emphasis, with the long s printed as s. Each exposition opens with its verse label and the words of the text it expounds, such as Verse 2. Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, and the paragraphs after it stay with its verse. Each exposition the transcription divides off is one section, keyed by the verse label printed at its head, such as Verse. 3, 4. or Verses 19, 20, 21., and running from its first verse to the verse before the next section or the end of its chapter, so a verse that one exposition shares with the next stays with the later one. The two volumes are read as one book: chapters 1 and 2 from the first, and chapters 3 to 5 from the second, whose chapters are numbered by their headings, such as 1 Ep. St. Peter Chap. III. A verse named in the exposition is never read. Every gap the transcribers could not key is kept as the mark they gave it, such as • for an illegible letter and 〈◊〉 for an illegible word. Line-end hyphens are closed up. Left out: the imprimatur, the title pages, the epistle to the pious reader, James Fall's epistle to the Christian reader, the list of Leighton's books, the errata, and the chapter headings such as Chap. Second.
